question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=2\sqrt[3]{3x-1}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=2\sqrt[3]{3x-1}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=2\sqrt[3]{3y-1}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2\sqrt[3]{3y-1} \\ \sqrt[3]{3y-1} & =\frac{1}{2}x \\ {(\sqrt[3]{3y-1})}^{3} & ={(\frac{1}{2}x)}^{3} \\ 3y-1 & =\frac{1}{8}{x}^{3} \\ 3y & =\frac{1}{8}{x}^{3}+1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{8}{x}^{3}+1) \\ y & =\frac{1}{24}({x}^{3}+8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{24}({x}^{3}+8).
$$
